newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday, issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
The central bank does not post volumes.
Traders said trading was more active today than last week but the rates continued to move in a narrow box.
"Demand and supply seemed balanced today, causing the rates to move little for the whole session," one trader said. "But the three-day contract was strong due to the firm A share market."

Traders said the rising domestic A share market was one major factor for active trading today. "Some financial institutions including securities houses borrowed funds to speculate in the A share market," said a second trader.
Shanghai's A share index ended up 5.94 percent to 893.55 points on Monday and the Shenzhen A index rose 0.17 percent.
